messages:
taylor.r: Hey all, Im Taylor (infra new hire). Trying to get a CI job running that does two things: 1) spins up a GKE job that writes formatted billing rows into our BigQuery 'billing_exports' dataset in project redwood-sbx, and 2) pushes built images to the org ECR repo in the shared infra AWS account. Whats the minimal set of perms I should request and who owns these on the infra side?
craig: welcome Taylor! :wave: For GCP: best practice is a dedicated SA in your sandbox project (eg billing-writer-sa@redwood-sbx.iam.gserviceaccount.com). Grant that SA BigQuery Data Editor on the specific dataset (not project-wide). Give your user roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator on that SA so CI runners can impersonate it.
samir: For GKE we use Workload Identity -> ensure you create a k8s service account (ksa) and bind it to the GCP SA. Open a cloud-access ticket with: project id, dataset name, k8s namespace + ksa, and whether this runs on ephemeral jobs or long-lived pods. Tag @oncall-cloud if its blocking a deploy.
infra-bot: Please use the cloud-access onboarding template: https://redwood.atlassian.net/secure/CreateIssue!default.jspa?project=CLOUD Choose 'Onboarding - IAM/Permissions' and include AWS account id, GCP project, dataset names, k8s details, and desired expiry.
anne: For AWS ECR pushes in the shared account we create a cross-account assume-role with a tight inline policy scoped to just the repo and registry actions. Minimal ECR push perms are: ecr:InitiateLayerUpload, ecr:UploadLayerPart, ecr:CompleteLayerUpload, ecr:PutImage, ecr:BatchCheckLayerAvailability, ecr:GetAuthorizationToken (if using auth). If artifacts are in S3, then s3:PutObject on the specific prefix.
craig: sample AWS trust policy we give infra to create the role (paste in ticket): ```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [{
    "Effect": "Allow",
    "Principal": {
      "AWS": "arn:aws:iam::ACCOUNT_ID:user/taylor.r@redwood.com"
    },
    "Action": "sts:AssumeRole"
  }]
}
```
(Infra will replace the Principal with a proper user or a federated principal depending on onboarding flow.)
samir: Concrete GCP commands to include in the ticket if you want infra to pre-provision: ```bash
# create SA
gcloud iam service-accounts create billing-writer-sa --project=redwood-sbx --display-name="billing writer"
# grant dataset access
bq add-iam-policy-binding redwood-sbx:billing_exports --member=serviceAccount:billing-writer-sa@redwood-sbx.iam.gserviceaccount.com --role=roles/bigquery.dataEditor
# allow you to impersonate SA
gcloud iam service-accounts add-iam-policy-binding billing-writer-sa@redwood-sbx.iam.gserviceaccount.com --member=user:taylor.r@redwood.com --role=roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator
```
taylor.r: thanks. whats the standard expiry window for onboarding perms? prefer temporary creds for CI while I validate things.
anne: Our standard onboarding window is 14 days for ephemeral CI/validation access. If you need longer we can request 60/90 days but youll need a justification in the ticket. Infra will add IAM conditions or issue time-limited role sessions.
craig: one gotcha: org policy blocks certain regions (asia-south1) for billing export buckets; mention preferred region in ticket. Also if you need logs exported, mention whether table schema needs to be permitted for insert via jobs.insert (you might also need roles/bigquery.jobUser for running load jobs).
infra-bot: Tip: include the CI runner identity (service account or Jenkins/GHA OIDC issuer) in the ticket so infra can configure trust.
taylor.r: filed CLOUD-1518 with project=redwood-sbx, dataset=billing_exports, k8s ns=ci-jobs, ksa=ci-billing-ksa, aws acct=123456789012, requested 14d expiry, noted region us-central1 and that CI uses OIDC. Appreciate the help! :smile:
